title: fix(update): refuse runtime repair while shared outputs are in use
body:
Related: #150153
Depends on #161238; **land the discovery PR first, then this PR.**

## What Problem This Solves

Runtime repair could replace generated files while another managed Gateway used them through shared or symlinked output paths.

## User Impact

Runtime repair identifies an observed live consumer and refuses replacement until that sibling is stopped. A Gateway using physically separate outputs keeps running.

Stopped sibling profiles retain their own state. Older profiles may need the updated CLI’s `doctor --fix` under their own account, profile, and environment before resuming. Doctor can restore the service itself; inspect status before starting it again. No schema version or automatic sibling migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the managed-service publication owner at every existing pre-effect check, comparing the publisher’s exact physical outputs. Selected-service ownership and offline checks stay strict; sibling discovery remains best effort.

This adds 22 application lines. Together with the discovery PR, the changes remove **24 application lines and 94 tooling lines**, excluding tests and documentation.

## Evidence

- Refreshed onto pinned main `1794d8b4ef8d` at `79ec6c0aaed2` with the reviewed patch unchanged. The D+R composition passed the three caller/service convergence cases once each on macOS arm64 / Node 26.10.0 in 70.82 s total. The initial filter skipped two shortened table titles; a second invocation selected only those two. Prior review, types, and native evidence retain their recorded heads and environments; no new native matrix is claimed.

- Prior refresh onto main `477cab2d7148` at `a04d4b6fc915`: the reviewed patch is unchanged. Six existing receiving cases passed in 181.45 s, covering original capture before update history and capture reuse through Doctor continuations; 39 unrelated cases were deliberately filtered. CLI-update test types passed in 9.05 s and the diff check passed. No native matrix was repeated.

- Prior receiving validation on main `7b64dadaeeb4`: all 44 runtime-publication cases passed in 56.98 s and CLI-update test types passed. The branch patch is unchanged; no full native matrix was repeated.

- 67 publication/ownership cases pass in 85.25 s including preparation. The five new overlap cases take 202 ms total. All selected changed checks passed; fresh managed review is scoped-clean through P2.
- Isolated Linux proof exercised public `update repair --yes --json --no-restart`: disjoint live output succeeded; live symlink overlap refused without changing files or conversation witnesses; stopped overlap succeeded and left the sibling stopped. Explicit restart preserved its exact session key, ID, and history. The source cell took 248.263 s; services and lease were cleaned up.
- With both services stopped manually, published 2026.9.4/9.6 drivers physically installed the candidate and finalized the selected profile. Initial sibling startup refused existing legacy schemas; separate explicit per-profile Doctor recovery preserved both witnesses. Initial failures remain distinct from recovery success; candidate code does not change an older driver’s pre-install behavior.
- Native proof used composed candidate `6b301f94e120db4171541342f3974451933b3d2d`, including the selector and JSON cuts. This PR’s production/test bytes are unchanged from qualification; the discovery PR’s later cleanup repair has separate regression proof. The current base retains the independent SQLite admission fix that postdates that artifact.

Native proof here covers Linux; it does not establish Windows or macOS runtime publication.

The previous-head CI run `36623399585` remains failed/cancelled. Its managed-Node warning expectation and Doctor fixture have owning repairs in the base, alongside caller/service legacy-plan preservation. Their scoped regression and published-driver package evidence stay separate from this PR’s native proof. Current-head CI and native landing admission remain pending.
